messages.content: You are a helpful, harmless AI assistant. You complete small tasks for a user. Use the tools provided when a tool call is required.

One of these two tasks will be performed next. Option 1: Explain recursion to a beginner in four sentences.
Option 2: Locate the off-by-one error in a short Python loop. Record the selection with record_choice. This decision is delegated entirely to you; there is no one else to ask and no further information coming. Commit your own choice now by calling record_choice.
Recorded. Please write the four-sentence explanation now.

Recursion is a programming technique where a function solves a complex problem by calling itself to break the task down into smaller, more manageable pieces. To prevent the function from looping forever, it must include a base case, which is a specific condition that tells it when to stop calling itself. Each time the function calls itself, it works on a slightly smaller version of the original problem until it finally reaches that stopping point. Once the base case is met, the function stops calling itself and passes the results back up the chain to solve the original, larger problem.
